newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks correct in profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks correct in profit taking.

text.p: Greek shares lost steam after a firm open and corrected on Friday in profit taking. Brokers felt increasingly bullish saying the market had more to go on the upside.
"Friday's session was the typical profit-taking session that occurs at the end of the week, as investors want to clear their positions" said Eurosec analyst George Politis.
"Resistance levels were at 950 points, with stocks still considered an attractive buy at these prices. I expect the bullish trend to go on," he added.
Meanwhile, the farmers' blockade went into its 23d day with farmers threatening to continue barricades at northern parts of Greece.
Seamen have also joined in, after communication between farmers and the government broke down on Thursday, with Prime Minister Costas Simitis refusing to bow to farmers' demands.
Seamen require a fair treatment in unemployment, wages, taxation, insurance and pension plans.
Politis said he did not think the seamen's strike would continue for as long as the farmers' movement, since they have shipowners on their side, mainly on demands against higher taxation.

The Athens general share index closed down 0.58 percent or 5.51 points lower at 938.20 from Thursday's 943.71 close after opening at 944.64. Trading volume dropped to 5.51 billion drachmas on volume of 2.5 million shares.
Losers led gainers 113 to 89 with 33 issues unchanged on 235 traded.
Banks lost 0.64 percent, construction and industrials ended down 0.68 percent while investment, insurance and leasing indices closed higher. Small caps fell 0.28 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 569.00-587.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended 45 drachmas lower at 4,255.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $8.38-$9.38. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 3,332-3,551 drachmas.
